ucl-lsgnt31.scope: 官方联合中心总表 69 条，按所列机构筛出 UCL 21 人。校外主聘和历史身份按各院正式个人页再核。

entries.name: Sougato Bose
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Sougato (Co-Director) investigates experimental protocols to test the quantum nature of gravity, in close collaboration with experimentalists cooling and levitating large masses.

entries.name: Jonathan Oppenheim
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Jonathan Oppenheim (Co-Director) explores an alternative to quantum gravity in which spacetime remains classical while quantum theory is modified, resulting in an intrinsic breakdown of predictability

entries.name: Peter Barker
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Peter Barker (Head of Experimental Research) cools, manipulates and transports atoms, molecules and nanoparticles in optical tweezers, and explores levitated nanomechanics for quantum sensing.

entries.name: Marika Taylor
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Marika Taylor (Executive Dean) works on quantum gravity, string theory and holography. She uses the holographic principle to explore black holes and quantum information.

entries.name: Christian Boehmer
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Christian Böehmer (Mathematics) studies general relativity and cosmology, focusing on alternative gravity theories that avoid singularities.

entries.name: Betti Hartmann
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Betti Hartmann (Mathematics) researches general relativity and field theory, focusing on black holes, solitons, and applications to astrophysics and cosmology.

entries.name: Rosemary Harris
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Rosemary Harris (Mathematics) studies stochastic non‑equilibrium processes, including interacting particle systems and large deviations.

entries.name: Rod Halburd
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Rod Halburd (Mathematics) works on integrable systems, the anti‑self‑dual Yang‑Mills equations, general relativity and complex analysis.

entries.name: Toby Cubitt
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Toby Cubitt (Physics & Astronomy) is interested in mathematically rigorous toy models of AdS/CFT duality and its connections to quantum error correction and Hamiltonian simulation.

entries.name: Lluis Masanes
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Lluis Masanes (Physics & Astronomy) is interested in discrete holography and quantum causality.

entries.name: Marzena Szymanska
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Marzena Szymanska (Physics & Astronomy) studies out-of-equilibrium phenomena in light–matter systems, including exciton-polaritons, cavity and circuit QED, and cold atoms.

entries.name: Andrew Green
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Andrew Green (Physics & Astronomy) researches correlated quantum systems, including tensor network models in AdS/CFT and both equilibrium and out-of-equilibrium strongly correlated phenomena.

entries.name: Clara Bradley
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Clara Bradley (Philosophy) is a lecturer whose research focuses on the philosophy of physics, particularly the structure of gauge theories and their Hamiltonian and Lagrangian formulations.

entries.name: Tania Monteiro
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Tania Monteiro (Physics & Astronomy) works at the interface of quantum and classical regimes and collaborates closely with experimentalists.

entries.name: Johannes Noller
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Johannes Noller (Physics & Astronomy) studies gravitational wave science, cosmology and particle physics, combining theoretical and data-driven methods and exploring dark energy.

entries.name: Alessio Serafini
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Alessio Serafini (Physics & Astronomy) specialises in quantum information with continuous variables, quantum optics and quantum control, including Gaussian states and quantum protocols.

entries.name: Ofer Lahav
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Ofer Lahav (Physics & Astronomy) is the Perren Chair of Astronomy, whose research focuses on observational cosmology, galaxy surveys and the nature of dark energy and dark matter.

entries.name: Emma Tobin
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Emma Tobin (Science & Technology Studies) is Professor of Philosophy of Science, working on the metaphysics of natural kinds and the philosophy of chemistry and biochemistry.

entries.name: Rory Jubber
entries.title: Center Affiliate · Quantum Information Science
entries.research: Rory Jubber (Science & Technology Studies) is a lecturer in the philosophy of science. His research focuses on the metaphysics of physical science and the social epistemology of science.

entries.name: Jun Maillard
entries.title: Academic Research Staff · Vědecký pracovník

entries.name: Josef Málek
entries.title: Professor · Profesor
entries.research: Analýza nelineárních parciálních diferenciálních rovnic, zejména rovnic popisujících mechanické, tepelné či chemické procesy v tekutinách, pevných látkách a směsích. Termodynamika a mechanika nenewtonských tekutin.

entries.name: Oleksandr Minakov
entries.title: Assistant Professor · Odborný asistent
entries.research: Integrovatelné parciální diferenciální rovnice: dlouhodobá asymptotická analýza problémů počáteční hodnoty s krokovými počátečními daty (Kortewegova - de Vriesova rovnice, Camassa - Holmova rovnice, nelineární Schrödingerova rovnice atd.). Přímé a inverzní rozptylové transformace pro neklesající a zvyšující se potenciály. Riemann-Hilbertovy problémy a asymptotické metody pro oscilační Riemann-Hilbertovy problémy. Další zájmy: ortogonální polynomy, Painlevé rovnice, náhodné matice.

entries.name: Vlasta Moravcová
entries.title: Lecturer · Lektor
entries.research: Didaktika matematiky, zejména geometrie; dějiny a didaktika deskriptivní geometrie; syntetická geometrie.

entries.name: Sebastian Opper
entries.title: Academic Research Staff · Vědecký pracovník

entries.name: Zuzana Patáková
entries.title: Assistant Professor · Odborný asistent
entries.research: Diskrétní a výpočetní geometrie, algebraická a topologická kombinatorika.

entries.name: Michal Pavelka
entries.title: Associate Professor · Docent
entries.research: Mé hlavní dva vědecké zájmy jsou: Geometrická nerovnovážná termodynamika a teoretická elektrochemie. V tom prvním typicky spojuji hamiltonovskou mechaniku s gradientní dynamikou, zatímco v tom druhém simuluji vodíkové palivové články a redoxní průtočné baterie. Vyučuji dva předměty, které tato témata obsahují.

entries.name: Réamonn Peadar Ó Buachalla
entries.title: Assistant Professor · Odborný asistent
entries.research: Můj výzkum se týká nekomutativní geometrie kvantových grup a jejich kvantových homogenních prostorů, zejména kvantové vlajkové variety. Pro svoji práci používám směs Hopfových algeber, monoidních kategorií, Lieovy teorie, komplexní a Kählerovy geometrie, C* -algeber a neomezené teorie operátorů.

entries.name: Luboš Pick
entries.title: Professor · Profesor

entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Mathew Bullimore
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research focuses on the mathematical structures underlying quantum field theory. I lead an ERC Consolidator grant developing the mathematical foundations of generalised symmetries, aiming to deepen our understanding of quantum systems.

entries.name: Stefano Cremonesi
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Quantum Field Theory, String Theory, Algebraic Geometry

entries.name: Aristomenis Donos
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research focuses on holography, black hole physics, and hydrodynamics in strongly coupled systems, investigating transport phenomena, symmetry breaking, and emergent dynamics in gravitational duals of quantum field theories.

entries.name: Patrick Dorey
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Conformal and integrable field theories

entries.name: Daniele Dorigoni
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Sam Fearn

entries.name: Iñaki García Etxebarria
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Quantum Field Theory, String Theory, Dualities, String Phenomenology

entries.name: Tobias Hansen
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research focuses on conformal field theories and string theory, combining ideas relating to conformal bootstrap, scattering amplitudes and AdS/CFT to further our understanding of string theories in curved spacetimes.

entries.name: Robie Hennigar
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: I study fundamental aspects of gravity and its interplay with quantum physics. My work covers the dynamics of black hole horizons, holographic descriptions of quantum black holes, and the fate of black hole interiors beyond general relativity.

entries.name: Paul Heslop
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Paul Heslop’s research explores quantum field theory and quantum gravity through the AdS/CFT correspondence, focusing on correlation functions and amplitudes to uncover hidden symmetries and geometric structures.

entries.name: Ben Hoare
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Integrability, deformations and dualities, and their applications to quantum field theory, string theory and gauge/gravity duality. Establishing new links with other topics, including quantum algebra and statistical physics.

entries.name: Nabil Iqbal
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Nabil has diverse interests, including the study of neural networks as physical systems, generalized global symmetries and their applications, holographic duality, and applications of quantum field theory to statistical physics.

entries.name: Polydoros Kailidis
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Holography, Effective field theory, Hydrodynamics

entries.name: Ayan Kumar Patra
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research primarily focuses on understanding black hole dynamics through the lens of holographic duality, specifically on how black hole interiors are encoded in the observables of the dual quantum field theory.

entries.name: Madalena Lemos
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Studying conformal and superconformal field theories, including local and extended operators (defects), through non-perturbative approaches such as bootstrap techniques and chiral algebras (vertex operator algebras) of superconformal field theories.

entries.name: Arthur Lipstein
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Quantum field theory, string theory, holography, and cosmology

entries.name: Maciej Matuszewski
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Automated e-assessment for undergraduate mathematics, String theory and the string/gauge theory correspondence, Pair production in quantum field theories.

entries.name: Paul McFadden
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research explores the implications of holography for early universe cosmology, and the development of momentum-space methods in conformal field theory.

entries.name: Silvia Nagy
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: I work on gravity as a double copy of gauge theory, including its mathematical underpinnings and extensions to curved spaces. I also study asymptotic symmetries and their applications to scattering amplitudes, and flat-space holography.

entries.name: Mendel Nguyen
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Non-perturbative quantum field theory

entries.name: Kasper Peeters
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: String theory and the string/gauge theory correspondence, Quantum gravity, Applications of mathematics to biology, Computer algebra

entries.name: Bernard Piette
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: I model some biological systems such as the cytoskeleton or the initial Darwin ancestor (proto-ribosme). I also study potential geometries for protein nano-cages via the classification of Polyhedral Cages.

entries.name: Simon Ross
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: I work on string theory and quantum gravity, focusing on the emergence of spacetime in holography and the description of black holes, using the gravitational path integral and entanglement.

entries.name: Tom Rudelius
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Tom Rudelius's research explores the intersection of string theory, cosmology, and quantum field theory, focussing on how theoretical constraints from quantum gravity shape models of the early universe and particle physics.

entries.name: Parita Shah
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research explores integrability and dualities in string theory, with emphasis on T-dualities and integrable sigma models, studying their holographic duals, and higher-derivative corrections to supergravity.

entries.name: Douglas Smith
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: String Theory, Supersymmetric Field Theories

entries.name: Luuk Stehouwer
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: I study mathematical aspects of QFT. I apply techniques from algebraic topology and category theory to understand TQFTs, topological phases of matter, and anomalies.

entries.name: Tin Sulejmanpasic
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Paul Sutcliffe

entries.name: Marija Zamaklar

entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Stochastic analysis, particularly rough path theory and its applications in stochastic filtering and mathematical finance.

entries.name: Irene Ayuso Ventura
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Sunil Chhita

entries.name: Nicholas Georgiou
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Probability theory and its applications; probabilistic models and stochastic processes; (random) processes on (random) graphs; spatial random graphs; probabilistic combinatorics.

entries.name: Tyler Helmuth
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Statistical mechanics, statistical field theory, and related problems in probability, combinatorics, and theoretical computer science.

entries.name: Ostap Hryniv
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Yao Jinxiang

entries.name: Mikhail Menshikov

entries.name: Ellen Powell

entries.name: Mustazee Rahman

entries.name: Oliver Tough
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Matthias Troffaes
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Andrew Wade
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Random walks and their geometry, stochastic processes with constraints or interactions, random spatial graphs, and systems of interacting particles.

entries.name: Clare Wallace
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: How students develop mathematical writing skills; whether peer assessment can help (and whether it’s a good thing anyway); how we talk about examples with students; and e-assessment (particularly STACK).

entries.name: Huaizhong Zhao
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Stochastic analysis; SPDEs; ergodic theory; dynamics of nonstationary processes; nonlinear expectations; optimal controls; large deviations; stochastic numerics; testing periodicity/quasi-periodicity in finite/infinite dimensions.

entries.name: Jonathan Cumming

entries.research: Hailiang works on statistical and machine-learning methods for uncertainty quantification, probabilistic forecasting, and nonlinear dynamical systems, with applications in weather and climate modelling, energy, and environmental resilience.

entries.name: Eimear Dunne
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Jochen Einbeck
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate

entries.name: Michael Goldstein
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Michael works on foundations, methods and applications of statistics and decision making, with particular emphasis on Bayes linear inference and Uncertainty Quantification for large computer models.

entries.name: Andrew Golightly
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Andrew works on Bayesian inference methodology for complex stochastic processes, including stochastic differential equations and jump processes, with applications in epidemiology, population ecology and systems biology.

entries.name: John Paul Gosling

entries.name: Sarah Heaps
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Sarah works primarily on Bayesian time-series analysis, latent variable modelling and the development of structured prior distributions. Her research is largely motivated by applications in the life sciences.

entries.name: Andrew Iskauskas
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Andrew works in uncertainty quantification and calibration for complex computer models, using Bayes Linear emulation and history matching, with applications in epidemiology and physics.

entries.name: Samuel Jackson
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Sam works on the Uncertainty Quantification, statistical analysis and Bayesian emulation of computer models, with applications including defence-threat reduction, epidemiology, physiology, systems biology and X-ray imaging.

entries.name: Ian Jermyn
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: My research focuses on applied and computational statistics, developing and applying Bayesian and Bayes linear methods for uncertainty analysis, emulation, and model assessment, with applications in engineering and environmental modelling.

entries.name: Sungkyung Kang
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Sungkyung’s research interests include survey methodology and multilevel model analysis using population-based data. She is also interested in interpreting quantitative and qualitative findings through social and cultural lenses.

entries.name: Georgios Karagiannis
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Georgios is a Bayesian statistician focused on statistical modelling, uncertainty quantification, spatial statistics, computational methods for complex models, and statistical machine learning.

entries.name: James Liley
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: James works mostly in theory and applications of predictive models, with a particular interest in making use of predictions in medical settings. He also has interests in high-dimensional statistics, data security, and clinical trials.

entries.name: Hyeyoung Maeng
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Hyeyoung works on change-point detection, dimension reduction, high-dimensional statistics, factor analysis and time series, with applications in finance and environment.

entries.name: Tahani Maturi
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Tahani works mainly on the development and application of nonparametric predictive inference, with further interests in reliability, survival analysis, diagnostic accuracy, and modelling dependence.

entries.name: Cuong Nguyen
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Cuong’s research includes methodology, theory, and applications of machine learning and artificial intelligence, with particular interests in the intersections of deep learning and statistics.

entries.name: Emmanuel Ogundimu
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Emmanuel's research focuses on variable selection, machine learning, and sample selection models, developing high-dimensional and semiparametric methods for rare-event data in biostatistics, clinical trials, credit scoring, and omics.

entries.name: Rachel Oughton
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Rachel’s main area of research is causal inference in controlled and observational studies, particularly in the social sciences. She is also interested in quantification of uncertainty in computer models, and is involved in several outreach projects.

entries.name: Ian Vernon
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Ian develops and applies Bayesian approaches to Uncertainty Quantification for the analysis of complex physical systems. Application areas include cosmology, epidemiology, nuclear physics, geology and systems biology.

entries.name: Darren Wilkinson
entries.title: Research Group Affiliate
entries.research: Darren uses computational Bayesian inference to study stochastic dynamical systems and other complex models. He works on substantive applications in fields such as systems biology and engineering.

entries.name: Nadima El-Hassan
entries.title: Visiting Scholar
entries.research: Nadima joined the School of Finance and Economics as a full-time staff member in July 1997. Her research interests include the pricing and hedging of complex derivatives, term structure modeling, risk management and portfolio attribution analysis. She has publications in a number of the leading international journals in finance including The Journal of Financial Engineering, Asian Capital Markets, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control and Journal of Computational Finance.

entries.name: Len Patrick Garces
entries.title: Visiting Scholar
entries.research: Len Patrick Garces is an applied mathematician whose research interests lie within the field of financial and actuarial mathematics, primarily on the applications of probability theory and stochastic analysis to tackle financial and actuarial problems (e.g. financial or insurance risk modelling and management, asset price modelling, term structure modelling, pricing and hedging financial derivatives) and the development of numerical and statistical methods to solve these problems.

entries.name: Hajra Khan
entries.title: Graduate Research Student
entries.research: My research focuses on developing advanced interfacial engineering strategies to improve the performance, stability, and lifespan of rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). Although zinc-ion batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage due to their inherent safety, cost-effectiveness, abundance, and environmental advantages, their practical application is hindered by challenges associated with zinc metal anodes. These include non-uniform zinc deposition, dendrite formation, hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and undesirable side reactions, which can compromise battery performance and cycling stability.

entries.name: Dongfang Li
entries.title: Graduate Research Student
entries.research: Dongfang Li is a PhD candidate in chemistry at the School of Mathematical and Physical Sciences at the University of Technology Sydney. His research focuses on advanced energy storage and conversion technologies, particularly CO₂ electroreduction and water-splitting electrolysis, with an emphasis on integrating Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) and their derivatives as functional materials. He has developed specialized expertise in synchrotron-based characterization techniques, including in-situ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) and Powder Diffraction (PD), as well as Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) and complementary in-situ/operando characterization methods.

entries.name: Chao Liu
entries.title: Research Assistant
entries.research: Dr. Chao Liu is a Postdoctoral Research Associate under the supervision of Prof. Guoxiu Wang in the Centre for Clean Energy Technology, University of Technology Sydney. His research interests include the synthesis of two-dimensional functional membrane materials for ion transport and energy conversion applications.

entries.name: Dayanne Mozaner Bordin
entries.title: Lecturer In Analytical Chemistry
entries.research: Dayanne Bordin is an analytical chemist and a member of the Atomic Medicine Initiative (AMI). Her research focuses on developing innovative mass spectrometry-based techniques for characterising small biomolecules, trace elements, proteomic bioindicators, and emerging nanomaterials in a forensic, biological, and clinical context.

entries.name: Connor Phillips
entries.title: Graduate Research Student
entries.research: Connor Phillips is an Associate Lecturer in the Faculty of Science at UTS. His teaching interests are primarily in the field of molecular biosciences including Molecular Biology and Metabolic Biochemistry. His research focuses on the analysis of non-protein amino acids that have been implicated in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative disorders such as multiple sclerosis using analytical chemistry techniques including LC-MS

entries.name: Alam Shabbir
entries.title: Graduate Research Student
entries.research: Mr Alam Shabbir is an Emerging Research Fellow of the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC EL1) and a Presidential Research Fellow (PRF) at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS), with expertise in organic synthesis, analytical chemistry, spectroscopic characterisations, and biomedical engineering. Currently, Mr Alam leads the research focusing on developing hybrid materials with desired functions, optical and nanophotonic properties, and integrating these new functionalities into molecular/nano-probes and functional devices for ultrasensitive bioassay, biomedical imaging, and precise therapy.

entries.name: S Nibedita Swain
entries.title: Graduate Research Student
entries.research: S Nibedita Swain is a full-time PhD candidate, funded by Sydney Quantum Academy, and currently a visiting scholar with Centre for Quantum Computation and Communication Technology, School of Mathematics and Physics, University of Queensland. Her research focuses on quantum computation and quantum error correction using optical systems. Specifically, in the direction of photonic architecture based on continuous variable systems ranging from quantum communication to quantum computation. entries.name: Emily Booth
entries.title: Research Fellow
entries.research: Emily Booth is a Research Fellow at the University of Technology in Sydney, Australia. She specialises in narratives, particularly as they manifest at part of misinformation, disinformation, and conspiracy theories; and has a particular interest in the narrative experiences of young people, offline and online. Her work seeks to address the underlying drivers of social discord rather than their surface-level expressions. At the intersection of social sciences and literary studies, she draws on the theoretical and methodological strengths for her transdisciplinary research.

entries.name: Steve Burdon
entries.title: Emeritus Professor
entries.research: Professor Steve Burdon AM (FIEAust, FAICD, FIMLA) research interests are Corporate Strategy, Innovation, Disruptive Technology, Digital Economy, Megaproject Management and Government Policy. He has recently been an Advisor to a number of leading Australian organisations including Telstra, Westpac and Transfield.

entries.name: Fang Chen
entries.title: Exec Director, Data Sci Institute & Distinguished Professor
entries.research: Research Expertise and Impact Areas

entries.name: Bogdan Gabrys
entries.title: Professor
entries.research: His research interests cover a broad range of intelligent and biologically/nature inspired learning and adaptive systems, as well as machine learning, statistical, and hybrid intelligent techniques encompassing data and information fusion, learning and adaptation methods, multiple classifier and prediction systems, robust optimisation approaches, processing and modelling of uncertainty in pattern recognition, diagnostic analysis and decision support systems.

entries.name: Thanh Tung Khuat
entries.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow
entries.research: Khuat's research interests include machine learning, interpretable machine learning, fuzzy systems, knowledge discovery, evolutionary computation, intelligent optimization techniques, and applications in software engineering.

entries.name: Jinyan Li
entries.title: Visiting Professor
entries.research: Jinyan is widely known for his pioneering and theoretical research work on Emerging Patterns that has spawned numerous follow-up research interests in data mining, machine learning, and bioinformatics and made an enduring contribution to these fields.

entries.name: Wei Liu
entries.title: Professor
entries.research: Wei is a Professor in Artificial Intelligence and the Director of the Future Intelligence Research Lab in the School of Computer Science at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS). He obtained his PhD degree in Machine Learning research at the University of Sydney (USYD). His current research focuses on LLM robustness, model hallucination, and multimodal machine learning.

entries.name: Simona Mihaita
entries.title: Associate Professor
entries.research: at the University of Technology Sydney| Data Science Institute. My research expertise lies in applied Artificial Intelligence for healthier and resilient smart cities, safer transport and e-mobility, and sustainable buildings.

entries.name: Catarina Pinto Moreira
entries.title: Associate Professor
entries.research: Dr. Catarina Moreira is a Computer Scientist and Engineer with extensive expertise in deep learning technologies and their societal impacts. She holds the position of Associate Professor in Machine Learning at the Data Science Institute, University of Technology Sydney. Her research interests comprise human-centered AI, multimodal deep learning, explainable AI, and probabilistic graphical models. Dr. Moreira is committed to advancing these fields while addressing their broader societal implications.

entries.name: Meera Radhakrishnan
entries.title: Visiting Fellow
entries.research: I am a Research Fellow at the Data Science Institute (DSI) at University of Technology Sydney (UTS). My core research interests lie in the areas of mobile and pervasive computing, multi-modal sensing systems using wearables & IoT devices embodied in the real-life space. I am passionate about research that explores practical solutions targeted at making a positive impact on the lifestyle of humans. My goal is to create innovative, human-centered systems that address global challenges while empowering individuals and communities.

entries.name: Bryan Zheng
entries.title: Research Assistant
entries.research: Bryan specializes in machine learning and explainable AI, participating in a diverse range of projects from industrial real estate data analysis to multidisciplinary research. He is skilled in using deep learning models to solve problems and employs explainable AI techniques for post-hoc analysis of model predictions. Currently, Bryan is involved in projects that connect agriculture with explainable AI and collaborates with Victor Chu.

entries.name: John P Davis
entries.title: Faculty
entries.research: Our group combines low-temperature physics with advanced nanofabrication and state-of-the art measurement techniques to explore a variety of physics. Roughly half of the group is focused on using cavity optomechanics to explore the quantum realm and produce new quantum technologies, and the other half on superfluids in restricted geometries (quasi-2D), but we also have many other projects including a superfluid gravitational wave/dark matter detector and advancing cryogenic techniques. Our students go on to exciting careers in quantum technology and top-notch post-docs.

entries.research: Performs multi-wavelength astronomical observations (with a focus on radio, millimetre, and X-ray observations), data mining, image processing, and statistical methods to: study the stellar undead (white dwarfs, neutron stars, and stellar-mass black holes that return to life by eating a nearby star) and supermassive black holes; learn how these objects produce highly-focused very-fast outflows (relativistic jets), as well as how jets affect their environment; reveal the foundations of the burgeoning field of multi-messenger astrophysics; and maximize discoveries within both wide-field and targetted time-domain astronomy.

entries.name: Michael Woodside

Methods: optical tweezers, single-molecule fluorescence, mass photometry, ligand-binding assays, simulation and modeling.

melb-stats26.scope: 直连 403，校方公开索引 Academic staff 段 25 位；与数学全名册和导师分组交叉。随机矩阵、统计形状和应用组分开。

melb-emeriti26.scope: 校级理学院公开荣休名单中两个具名数学学者卡，与纯数学和拓扑组及院士资料交叉。

melb-analysis26.scope: 官方独立组站人员：现任教员三位、具名博士后一位，另列当期及过去博士学生。公开个人档用于核对任职变化。

melb-matrix-gov26.scope: 直接读取治理名录及 Advisory Board、公开联系名单。Jan de Gier 为墨大主任，其他院校合作管理按各自主聘；住宿科研活动参加者为短访。

melb-matrix-exec26.scope: 机构公布三位主任及协调员。合作机构身份与墨大长聘分开，短访使用具体公开项目和日期。

melb-topology-visitors26.scope: 拓扑组具名访客页分时间列短访，和研究组 Members、Emeritus、Related Areas 分列。

melb-macsys26.scope: 联合研究中心直接访问 TLS EOF；中心公开成员索引及本人当前主页同时确认 MACSYS 的墨大博士后。

melb-vicgap26.scope: 联合网络连接墨大、Monash、La Trobe 等，各成员身份回到所属大学；跨校研讨会参加不作为任职依据。

melb-mathphys26.scope: 直连 403，公开索引可读到具名分组片段，索引正文请求超时。以学院 2026 公开研究手册、数学师资和物理官方分栏及个人网站逐名交叉；独立数学物理全页待验证。

melb-applied26.scope: 旧路径转至现行专题入口，People 子页直连 403，校方索引读取不稳定。以学院主名录的 Applied Mathematics and Mathematical Biology 标签、导师表及学者本人站交叉。

melb-discrete26.scope: 具名 People 页直连 403、公开索引超时；学科首页及主名录的研究分组、现任导师表和本人学术页用于交叉。

melb-edu26.scope: 直连 403、公开索引有栏目名。对照院系职级、研究招生手册及教育组具名研究，如拓扑研究者 TriThang Tran。

melb-topology26.scope: 检查拓扑组的 Members、Emeritus Members 及 Researchers in Related Areas 分栏，交叉几何结构与纯拓扑方向。

melb-reptheory26.scope: 直接核对数学表示论组具名档、现行研究方向及各自论文。代数簇的奇点与层、几何表示论文及数学物理应用分开。

melb-prospectus26.scope: 机构 PDF 直连 403，公开索引可读关键具名节。与当前学校名录、招生导师及跨院物理职务核对。

melb-phys-theory26.scope: 直连 403，已使用物理学院三分栏全名册、数学物理公开手册及具名机构档交叉。

melb-matrix-about26.scope: 研究所本身为多校合作住宅式科研项目，现任岗位依具名成员所在院系，短期访问由各项目时间和主职来源确定。
